# Tetrahedral quadrilateral sections: exact equations and an envelope obstruction

This supplies exact formulas for a proper section with two tetrahedron
vertices on each side. It also disproves the stronger claim that the
vertex-only weighted mean is a lower bound after such sections are
allowed. The exhibited weighted mean remains above γ_3=27/64; it is
not a counterexample to the desired γ_3 inequality.

## 1. Geometric formulas without a limiting divided-difference convention

Take the standard tetrahedron with vertices v_0=0, v_1=e_1,
v_2=e_2, v_3=e_3 and barycentric coordinates ξ_0,...,ξ_3. For
p,q,r,s>0 consider the cap

    p ξ_0+q ξ_1−r ξ_2−s ξ_3≥0.                         (1)

Its section has cyclic vertices A,B,C,D with barycentrics

    A=(r/(p+r),0,p/(p+r),0),
    B=(s/(p+s),0,0,p/(p+s)),
    C=(0,s/(q+s),0,q/(q+s)),
    D=(0,r/(q+r),q/(q+r),0).

Define

    α=ps/((p+r)(p+s)(q+s)),
    δ=qr/((p+r)(q+s)(q+r)),
    τ=α/(α+δ).

The cross products of triangles ABC and ACD are respectively −α n
and −δ n, where the raw continuous cap normal is

    n=(q−p,−r−p,−s−p).

This follows by direct substitution of the displayed edge intersections.
In particular their area ratio is α:δ. The section centroid λ is

    λ=(A+C+τB+(1−τ)D)/3.                               (2)

Explicitly,

    3λ_0=r/(p+r)+τs/(p+s),
    3λ_1=s/(q+s)+(1−τ)r/(q+r),
    3λ_2=p/(p+r)+(1−τ)q/(q+r),
    3λ_3=q/(q+s)+τp/(p+s).

The normalized coarea section mass, meaning the section area divided
by ||n|| and by the tetrahedron volume 1/6, is

    S=3(α+δ).                                          (3)

The normalized cap volume is

    F=p(α+δ)+q²/((q+s)(q+r)).                           (4)

For a proof of (4), triangulate the cap from v_0. The three tetrahedra
have opposite triangles ABC, ACD, and v_1CD. Their volume fractions
are respectively pα, pδ, and q²/((q+s)(q+r)), computed by three-by-three
determinants. Their interiors are disjoint and they cover the cap:
these are precisely the pyramids over the cap facets not containing
v_0. Formulas (2)–(4) remain valid when p=q or r=s; no denominators
vanish.

For comparison, if the four signed vertex values t_i are distinct,
one may write F=Σ_{t_i>0} t_i³/∏_{j≠i}(t_i−t_j). Its derivatives obey
∂F/∂t_i=Sλ_i and Σ_i∂F/∂t_i=S. The geometric formulas above are a
self-contained way to evaluate the same data even at repeated values.

## 2. The stronger vertex-cap envelope

Suppose λ_i<1/3, so all four vertex-isolating centroid sections exist.
Write P_λ=∏λ_i, D_λ=1−3Σλ_i², and

    R=27P_λ/D_λ.

The vertex-only balanced mean equals R. Let q_i be the vector equal
to normalized coarea section mass times raw normal for vertex cap i,
and let f_i=27P_λ/λ_i. There is an affine supporting functional

    f_i=R+v·q_i,
    v_k=λ_k(Σ_iλ_i²−λ_k)/D_λ,  k=1,2,3.                (5)

Substitution of the vertex raw margins proves (5). For the additional
quadrilateral cap (1), its analogous vector is Q=Sn. Since its
section centroid is λ, Σ_iλ_i t_i=0 and therefore

    v·Q=−S Σ_iλ_i²t_i/D_λ.

Thus the condition that this extra cap lie above the same vertex
supporting functional would be

    D_λ F+SΣ_iλ_i²t_i−27P_λ≥0.                         (6)

The complementary cap would require the corresponding expression
D_λ(1−F)−SΣ_iλ_i²t_i−27P_λ≥0. These stronger inequalities are false.

## 3. Exact rational obstruction

Choose

    (p,q,r,s)=(6,7,24,6),   t=(6,7,−24,−6).

Equations (2)–(4) give

    λ=(851/2610, 11218/35061, 4657/40455, 1621/6786),
    S=261/4030,   F=506/2015.

All four λ_i lie strictly between zero and 1/3. For this example,
the left side of the complementary version of (6) is exactly

    −76232299376/232609319856225 < 0.                   (7)

Here is a direct balanced-circuit certificate, not just a dual slack.
Use the complementary quadrilateral cap −Q and vertex-side caps
V_0,V_1,V_2. Give them the following probability weights, with common
denominator N=52425025485892802:

    θ_{−Q}=23097356755453943/N,
    θ_{V0}=13014678602879811/N,
    θ_{V1}=15094034160118200/N,
    θ_{V2}=1218955967440848/N.                            (8)

They are positive and sum to one. Their normalized coarea-normal
vectors are

    q_{−Q}=(-261/4030, 783/403, 1566/2015),
    q_{V0}=(-7548997/10167690, -9092189/4405999,
             -52242226/52533065),
    q_{V1}=(7548997/10167690, -9221869/6778460,
             -79169/292175),
    q_{V2}=(-10395473/264359940, 9092189/4405999,
             -572118/759655).

Direct rational substitution gives Σ θ_i q_i=0. Every section has
the same centroid λ: this is (2) for the quadrilateral and formula
t_j=3λ_j for the three triangular vertex sections. Their cap fractions
are respectively

    1509/2015,
    42342324173/178244689545,
    6424196447/26537670900,
    7737452839/11499657390.

The weighted mean is exactly

    12431494665571935/26212512742946401
        ≈0.47425803041019643,

whereas the vertex-only mean at this same centroid is

    36033317871223/75836660403033
        ≈0.4751437850733982.

The first value is strictly smaller, as certified by (7) or direct
cross multiplication. Its gap above the required constant is

    mean−27/64=87877814537051013/1677600815548569664>0.

Thus the full tetrahedral problem cannot be proved merely by declaring
all additional sections to lie above the exact vertex-only envelope.
The weaker universal lower bound 27/64 is not refuted here.
